bsb.10:24: Therefore this is what the Lord GOD of Hosts says: “O My people who dwell in Zion, do not fear Assyria, who strikes you with a rod and lifts his staff against you as the Egyptians did.
bsb.10:25: For in just a little while My fury against you will subside, and My anger will turn to their destruction.”
bsb.10:26: And the LORD of Hosts will brandish a whip against them, as when He struck Midian at the rock of Oreb. He will raise His staff over the sea, as He did in Egypt.
bsb.10:27: On that day the burden will be lifted from your shoulders, and the yoke from your neck. The yoke will be broken because your neck will be too large.
bsb.10:28: Assyria has entered Aiath and passed through Migron, storing their supplies at Michmash.
bsb.10:29: They have crossed at the ford: “We will spend the night at Geba.” Ramah trembles; Gibeah of Saul flees.
bsb.10:30: Cry aloud, O Daughter of Gallim! Listen, O Laishah! O wretched Anathoth!
bsb.10:31: Madmenah flees; the people of Gebim take refuge.
bsb.10:32: Yet today they will halt at Nob, shaking a fist at the mount of Daughter Zion, at the hill of Jerusalem.
bsb.10:33: Behold, the Lord GOD of Hosts will lop off the branches with terrifying power. The tall trees will be cut down, the lofty ones will be felled.
bsb.10:34: He will clear the forest thickets with an axe, and Lebanon will fall before the Mighty One.
bsb.11:1: Then a shoot will spring up from the stump of Jesse, and a Branch from his roots will bear fruit.
bsb.11:2: The Spirit of the LORD will rest on Him— the Spirit of wisdom and understanding, the Spirit of counsel and strength, the Spirit of knowledge and fear of the LORD.
bsb.11:3: And He will delight in the fear of the LORD. He will not judge by what His eyes see, and He will not decide by what His ears hear,
bsb.11:4: but with righteousness He will judge the poor, and with equity He will decide for the lowly of the earth. He will strike the earth with the rod of His mouth and slay the wicked with the breath of His lips.
bsb.11:5: Righteousness will be the belt around His hips, and faithfulness the sash around His waist.
bsb.11:6: The wolf will live with the lamb, and the leopard will lie down with the goat; the calf and young lion and fatling will be together, and a little child will lead them.
bsb.11:7: The cow will graze with the bear, their young will lie down together, and the lion will eat straw like the ox.
bsb.11:8: The infant will play by the cobra’s den, and the toddler will reach into the viper’s nest.
bsb.11:9: They will neither harm nor destroy on all My holy mountain, for the earth will be full of the knowledge of the LORD as the sea is full of water.
bsb.11:10: On that day the Root of Jesse will stand as a banner for the peoples. The nations will seek Him, and His place of rest will be glorious.
bsb.11:11: On that day the Lord will extend His hand a second time to recover the remnant of His people from Assyria, from Egypt, from Pathros, from Cush, from Elam, from Shinar, from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea.
bsb.11:12: He will raise a banner for the nations and gather the exiles of Israel; He will collect the scattered of Judah from the four corners of the earth.
bsb.11:13: Then the jealousy of Ephraim will depart, and the adversaries of Judah will be cut off. Ephraim will no longer envy Judah, nor will Judah harass Ephraim.
bsb.11:14: They will swoop down on the slopes of the Philistines to the west; together they will plunder the sons of the east. They will lay their hands on Edom and Moab, and the Ammonites will be subject to them.
bsb.11:15: The LORD will devote to destruction the gulf of the Sea of Egypt; with a scorching wind He will sweep His hand over the Euphrates. He will split it into seven streams for men to cross with dry sandals.
bsb.11:16: There will be a highway for the remnant of His people who remain from Assyria, as there was for Israel when they came up from the land of Egypt.
bsb.12:1: In that day you will say: “O LORD, I will praise You. Although You were angry with me, Your anger has turned away, and You have comforted me.
bsb.12:2: Surely God is my salvation; I will trust and not be afraid. For the LORD GOD is my strength and my song, and He also has become my salvation.”
bsb.12:3: With joy you will draw water from the springs of salvation,
bsb.12:4: and on that day you will say: “Give praise to the LORD; proclaim His name! Make His works known among the peoples; declare that His name is exalted.
bsb.12:5: Sing to the LORD, for He has done glorious things. Let this be known in all the earth.
bsb.12:6: Cry out and sing, O citizen of Zion, for great among you is the Holy One of Israel.”
bsb.13:1: This is the burden against Babylon that Isaiah son of Amoz received:
bsb.13:2: Raise a banner on a barren hilltop; call aloud to them. Wave your hand, that they may enter the gates of the nobles.
bsb.13:3: I have commanded My sanctified ones; I have even summoned My warriors to execute My wrath and exult in My triumph.
bsb.13:4: Listen, a tumult on the mountains, like that of a great multitude! Listen, an uproar among the kingdoms, like nations gathered together! The LORD of Hosts is mobilizing an army for war.
bsb.13:5: They are coming from faraway lands, from the ends of the heavens— the LORD and the weapons of His wrath— to destroy the whole country.
bsb.13:6: Wail, for the Day of the LORD is near; it will come as destruction from the Almighty.
bsb.13:7: Therefore all hands will fall limp, and every man’s heart will melt.
bsb.13:8: Terror, pain, and anguish will seize them; they will writhe like a woman in labor. They will look at one another, their faces flushed with fear.
bsb.13:9: Behold, the Day of the LORD is coming— cruel, with fury and burning anger— to make the earth a desolation and to destroy the sinners within it.
bsb.13:10: For the stars of heaven and their constellations will not give their light. The rising sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light.
bsb.13:11: I will punish the world for its evil and the wicked for their iniquity. I will end the haughtiness of the arrogant and lay low the pride of the ruthless.
bsb.13:12: I will make man scarcer than pure gold, and mankind rarer than the gold of Ophir.
bsb.13:13: Therefore I will make the heavens tremble, and the earth will be shaken from its place at the wrath of the LORD of Hosts on the day of His burning anger.
bsb.13:14: Like a hunted gazelle, like a sheep without a shepherd, each will return to his own people, each will flee to his native land.
bsb.13:15: Whoever is caught will be stabbed, and whoever is captured will die by the sword.
bsb.13:16: Their infants will be dashed to pieces before their eyes, their houses will be looted, and their wives will be ravished.
bsb.13:17: Behold, I will stir up against them the Medes, who have no regard for silver and no desire for gold.
bsb.13:18: Their bows will dash young men to pieces; they will have no mercy on the fruit of the womb; they will not look with pity on the children.
bsb.13:19: And Babylon, the jewel of the kingdoms, the glory of the pride of the Chaldeans, will be overthrown by God like Sodom and Gomorrah.
bsb.13:20: She will never be inhabited or settled from generation to generation; no nomad will pitch his tent there, no shepherd will rest his flock there.
bsb.13:21: But desert creatures will lie down there, and howling creatures will fill her houses. Ostriches will dwell there, and wild goats will leap about.
bsb.13:22: Hyenas will howl in her fortresses and jackals in her luxurious palaces. Babylon’s time is at hand, and her days will not be prolonged.
bsb.14:1: For the LORD will have compassion on Jacob; once again He will choose Israel and settle them in their own land. The foreigner will join them and unite with the house of Jacob.
bsb.14:2: The nations will escort Israel and bring it to its homeland. Then the house of Israel will possess the nations as menservants and maidservants in the LORD’s land. They will make captives of their captors and rule over their oppressors.
bsb.14:3: On the day that the LORD gives you rest from your pain and torment, and from the hard labor into which you were forced,
bsb.14:4: you will sing this song of contempt against the king of Babylon: How the oppressor has ceased, and how his fury has ended!
bsb.14:5: The LORD has broken the staff of the wicked, the scepter of the rulers.
bsb.14:6: It struck the peoples in anger with unceasing blows; it subdued the nations in rage with relentless persecution.
bsb.14:7: All the earth is at peace and at rest; they break out in song.
bsb.14:8: Even the cypresses and cedars of Lebanon exult over you: “Since you have been laid low, no woodcutter comes against us.”
bsb.14:9: Sheol beneath is eager to meet you upon your arrival. It stirs the spirits of the dead to greet you— all the rulers of the earth. It makes all the kings of the nations rise from their thrones.
bsb.14:10: They will all respond to you, saying, “You too have become weak, as we are; you have become like us!”
bsb.14:11: Your pomp has been brought down to Sheol, along with the music of your harps. Maggots are your bed and worms your blanket.
bsb.14:12: How you have fallen from heaven, O day star, son of the dawn! You have been cut down to the ground, O destroyer of nations.
bsb.14:13: You said in your heart: “I will ascend to the heavens; I will raise my throne above the stars of God. I will sit on the mount of assembly, in the far reaches of the north.
bsb.14:14: I will ascend above the tops of the clouds; I will make myself like the Most High.”
bsb.14:15: But you will be brought down to Sheol, to the lowest depths of the Pit.
bsb.14:16: Those who see you will stare; they will ponder your fate: “Is this the man who shook the earth and made the kingdoms tremble,
bsb.14:17: who turned the world into a desert and destroyed its cities, who refused to let the captives return to their homes?”
bsb.14:18: All the kings of the nations lie in state, each in his own tomb.
bsb.14:19: But you are cast out of your grave like a rejected branch, covered by those slain with the sword, and dumped into a rocky pit like a carcass trampled underfoot.
bsb.14:20: You will not join them in burial, since you have destroyed your land and slaughtered your own people. The offspring of the wicked will never again be mentioned.
bsb.14:21: Prepare a place to slaughter his sons for the iniquities of their forefathers. They will never rise up to possess a land or cover the earth with their cities.
bsb.14:22: “I will rise up against them,” declares the LORD of Hosts. “I will cut off from Babylon her name and her remnant, her offspring and her posterity,” declares the LORD.
bsb.14:23: “I will make her a place for owls and for swamplands; I will sweep her away with the broom of destruction,” declares the LORD of Hosts.
bsb.14:24: The LORD of Hosts has sworn: “Surely, as I have planned, so will it be; as I have purposed, so will it stand.
bsb.14:25: I will break Assyria in My land; I will trample him on My mountain. His yoke will be taken off My people, and his burden removed from their shoulders.”
bsb.14:26: This is the plan devised for the whole earth, and this is the hand stretched out over all the nations.
bsb.14:27: The LORD of Hosts has purposed, and who can thwart Him? His hand is outstretched, so who can turn it back?
bsb.14:28: In the year that King Ahaz died, this burden was received:
bsb.14:29: Do not rejoice, all you Philistines, that the rod that struck you is broken. For a viper will spring from the root of the snake, and a flying serpent from its egg.
bsb.14:30: Then the firstborn of the poor will find pasture, and the needy will lie down in safety, but I will kill your root by famine, and your remnant will be slain.
bsb.14:31: Wail, O gate! Cry out, O city! Melt away, all you Philistines! For a cloud of smoke comes from the north, and there are no stragglers in its ranks.
bsb.14:32: What answer will be given to the envoys of that nation? “The LORD has founded Zion, where His afflicted people will find refuge.”
bsb.15:1: This is the burden against Moab: Ar in Moab is ruined, destroyed in a night! Kir in Moab is devastated, destroyed in a night!
bsb.15:2: Dibon goes up to its temple to weep at its high places. Moab wails over Nebo, as well as over Medeba. Every head is shaved, every beard is cut off.
bsb.15:3: In its streets they wear sackcloth; on the rooftops and in the public squares they all wail, falling down weeping.
bsb.15:4: Heshbon and Elealeh cry out; their voices are heard as far as Jahaz. Therefore the soldiers of Moab cry out; their souls tremble within.
bsb.15:5: My heart cries out over Moab; her fugitives flee as far as Zoar, as far as Eglath-shelishiyah. With weeping they ascend the slope of Luhith; they lament their destruction on the road to Horonaim.
bsb.15:6: The waters of Nimrim are dried up, and the grass is withered; the vegetation is gone, and the greenery is no more.
bsb.15:7: So they carry their wealth and belongings over the Brook of the Willows.
bsb.15:8: For their outcry echoes to the border of Moab. Their wailing reaches Eglaim; it is heard in Beer-elim.
bsb.15:9: The waters of Dimon are full of blood, but I will bring more upon Dimon— a lion upon the fugitives of Moab and upon the remnant of the land.
bsb.16:1: Send the tribute lambs to the ruler of the land, from Sela in the desert to the mount of Daughter Zion.
bsb.16:2: Like fluttering birds pushed out of the nest, so are the daughters of Moab at the fords of the Arnon:
bsb.16:3: “Give us counsel; render a decision. Shelter us at noonday with shade as dark as night. Hide the refugees; do not betray the one who flees.
bsb.16:4: Let my fugitives stay with you; be a refuge for Moab from the destroyer.” When the oppressor has gone, destruction has ceased, and the oppressors have vanished from the land,
bsb.16:5: in loving devotion a throne will be established in the tent of David. A judge seeking justice and hastening righteousness will sit on it in faithfulness.
bsb.16:6: We have heard of Moab’s pomposity, his exceeding pride and conceit, his overflowing arrogance. But his boasting is empty.
bsb.16:7: Therefore let Moab wail; let them wail together for Moab. Moan for the raisin cakes of Kir-hareseth, you who are utterly stricken.
bsb.16:8: For the fields of Heshbon have withered, along with the grapevines of Sibmah. The rulers of the nations have trampled its choicest vines, which had reached as far as Jazer and spread toward the desert. Their shoots had spread out and passed over the sea.
bsb.16:9: So I weep with Jazer for the vines of Sibmah; I drench Heshbon and Elealeh with my tears. Triumphant shouts have fallen silent over your summer fruit and your harvest.
bsb.16:10: Joy and gladness are removed from the orchard; no one sings or shouts in the vineyards. No one tramples the grapes in the winepresses; I have put an end to the cheering.
bsb.16:11: Therefore my heart laments for Moab like a harp, my inmost being for Kir-heres.
bsb.16:12: When Moab appears on the high place, when he wearies himself and enters his sanctuary to pray, it will do him no good.
bsb.16:13: This is the message that the LORD spoke earlier concerning Moab.
bsb.16:14: And now the LORD says, “In three years, as a hired worker counts the years, Moab’s splendor will become an object of contempt, with all her many people. And those who are left will be few and feeble.”
bsb.17:1: This is the burden against Damascus: “Behold, Damascus is no longer a city; it has become a heap of ruins.
bsb.17:2: The cities of Aroer are forsaken; they will be left to the flocks, which will lie down with no one to fear.
bsb.17:3: The fortress will disappear from Ephraim, and the sovereignty from Damascus. The remnant of Aram will be like the splendor of the Israelites,” declares the LORD of Hosts.
bsb.17:4: “In that day the splendor of Jacob will fade, and the fat of his body will waste away,
bsb.17:5: as the reaper gathers the standing grain and harvests the ears with his arm, as one gleans heads of grain in the Valley of Rephaim.
bsb.17:6: Yet gleanings will remain, like an olive tree that has been beaten— two or three berries atop the tree, four or five on its fruitful branches,” declares the LORD, the God of Israel.
bsb.17:7: In that day men will look to their Maker and turn their eyes to the Holy One of Israel.
bsb.17:8: They will not look to the altars they have fashioned with their hands or to the Asherahs and incense altars they have made with their fingers.
bsb.17:9: In that day their strong cities will be like forsaken thickets and summits, abandoned to the Israelites and to utter desolation.
bsb.17:10: For you have forgotten the God of your salvation and failed to remember the Rock of your refuge. Therefore, though you cultivate delightful plots and set out cuttings from exotic vines—
bsb.17:11: though on the day you plant you make them grow, and on that morning you help your seed sprout— yet the harvest will vanish on the day of disease and incurable pain.
bsb.17:12: Alas, the tumult of many peoples; they rage like the roaring seas and clamoring nations; they rumble like the crashing of mighty waters.
bsb.17:13: The nations rage like the rush of many waters. He rebukes them, and they flee far away, driven before the wind like chaff on the hills, like tumbleweeds before a gale.
bsb.17:14: In the evening, there is sudden terror! Before morning, they are no more! This is the portion of those who loot us and the lot of those who plunder us.
bsb.18:1: Woe to the land of whirring wings, along the rivers of Cush,
bsb.18:2: which sends couriers by sea, in papyrus vessels on the waters. Go, swift messengers, to a people tall and smooth-skinned, to a people widely feared, to a powerful nation of strange speech, whose land is divided by rivers.
bsb.18:3: All you people of the world and dwellers of the earth, when a banner is raised on the mountains, you will see it; when a ram’s horn sounds, you will hear it.
bsb.18:4: For this is what the LORD has told me: “I will quietly look on from My dwelling place, like shimmering heat in the sunshine, like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest.”
bsb.18:5: For before the harvest, when the blossom is gone and the flower becomes a ripening grape, He will cut off the shoots with a pruning knife and remove and discard the branches.
bsb.18:6: They will all be left to the mountain birds of prey, and to the beasts of the land. The birds will feed on them in summer, and all the wild animals in winter.
bsb.18:7: At that time gifts will be brought to the LORD of Hosts— from a people tall and smooth-skinned, from a people widely feared, from a powerful nation of strange speech, whose land is divided by rivers— to Mount Zion, the place of the Name of the LORD of Hosts.
bsb.19:1: This is the burden against Egypt: Behold, the LORD rides on a swift cloud; He is coming to Egypt. The idols of Egypt will tremble before Him, and the hearts of the Egyptians will melt within them.
bsb.19:2: “So I will incite Egyptian against Egyptian; brother will fight against brother, neighbor against neighbor, city against city, and kingdom against kingdom.
bsb.19:3: Then the spirit of the Egyptians will be emptied out from among them, and I will frustrate their plans, so that they will resort to idols and spirits of the dead, to mediums and spiritists.
bsb.19:4: I will deliver the Egyptians into the hands of harsh masters, and a fierce king will rule over them,” declares the Lord GOD of Hosts.
bsb.19:5: The waters of the Nile will dry up, and the riverbed will be parched and empty.
bsb.19:6: The canals will stink; the streams of Egypt will trickle and dry up; the reeds and rushes will wither.
bsb.19:7: The bulrushes by the Nile, by the mouth of the river, and all the fields sown along the Nile, will wither, blow away, and be no more.
bsb.19:8: Then the fishermen will mourn, all who cast a hook into the Nile will lament, and those who spread nets on the waters will pine away.
bsb.19:9: The workers in flax will be dismayed, and the weavers of fine linen will turn pale.
bsb.19:10: The workers in cloth will be dejected, and all the hired workers will be sick at heart.
bsb.19:11: The princes of Zoan are mere fools; Pharaoh’s wise counselors give senseless advice. How can you say to Pharaoh, “I am one of the wise, a son of eastern kings”?
bsb.19:12: Where are your wise men now? Let them tell you and reveal what the LORD of Hosts has planned against Egypt.
bsb.19:13: The princes of Zoan have become fools; the princes of Memphis are deceived. The cornerstones of her tribes have led Egypt astray.
bsb.19:14: The LORD has poured into her a spirit of confusion. Egypt has been led astray in all she does, as a drunkard staggers through his own vomit.
bsb.19:15: There is nothing Egypt can do— head or tail, palm or reed.
bsb.19:16: In that day the Egyptians will be like women. They will tremble with fear beneath the uplifted hand of the LORD of Hosts, when He brandishes it against them.
bsb.19:17: The land of Judah will bring terror to Egypt; whenever Judah is mentioned, Egypt will tremble over what the LORD of Hosts has planned against it.
bsb.19:18: In that day five cities in the land of Egypt will speak the language of Canaan and swear allegiance to the LORD of Hosts. One of them will be called the City of the Sun.
bsb.19:19: In that day there will be an altar to the LORD in the center of the land of Egypt, and a pillar to the LORD near her border.
bsb.19:20: It will be a sign and a witness to the LORD of Hosts in the land of Egypt. When they cry out to the LORD because of their oppressors, He will send them a savior and defender to rescue them.
bsb.19:21: The LORD will make Himself known to Egypt, and on that day Egypt will acknowledge the LORD. They will worship with sacrifices and offerings; they will make vows to the LORD and fulfill them.
bsb.19:22: And the LORD will strike Egypt with a plague; He will strike them but heal them. They will turn to the LORD, and He will hear their prayers and heal them.
bsb.19:23: In that day there will be a highway from Egypt to Assyria. The Assyrians will go to Egypt, and the Egyptians to Assyria. The Egyptians and Assyrians will worship together.
bsb.19:24: In that day Israel will join a three-party alliance with Egypt and Assyria—a blessing upon the earth.
bsb.19:25: The LORD of Hosts will bless them, saying, “Blessed be Egypt My people, Assyria My handiwork, and Israel My inheritance.”
bsb.20:1: Before the year that the chief commander, sent by Sargon king of Assyria, came to Ashdod and attacked and captured it,
bsb.20:2: the LORD had already spoken through Isaiah son of Amoz, saying, “Go, remove the sackcloth from your waist and the sandals from your feet.” And Isaiah did so, walking around naked and barefoot.
bsb.20:3: Then the LORD said, “Just as My servant Isaiah has gone naked and barefoot for three years as a sign and omen against Egypt and Cush,
bsb.20:4: so the king of Assyria will lead away the captives of Egypt and the exiles of Cush, young and old alike, naked and barefoot, with bared buttocks—to Egypt’s shame.
bsb.20:5: Those who made Cush their hope and Egypt their boast will be dismayed and ashamed.
bsb.20:6: And on that day the dwellers of this coastland will say, ‘See what has happened to our source of hope, those to whom we fled for help and deliverance from the king of Assyria! How then can we escape?’”
bsb.21:1: This is the burden against the Desert by the Sea: Like whirlwinds sweeping through the Negev, an invader comes from the desert, from a land of terror.
bsb.21:2: A dire vision is declared to me: “The traitor still betrays, and the destroyer still destroys. Go up, O Elam! Lay siege, O Media! I will put an end to all her groaning.”
bsb.21:3: Therefore my body is filled with anguish. Pain grips me, like the pains of a woman in labor. I am bewildered to hear, I am dismayed to see.
bsb.21:4: My heart falters; fear makes me tremble. The twilight of my desire has turned to horror.
bsb.21:5: They prepare a table, they lay out a carpet, they eat, they drink! Rise up, O princes, oil the shields!
bsb.21:6: For this is what the Lord says to me: “Go, post a lookout and have him report what he sees.
bsb.21:7: When he sees chariots with teams of horsemen, riders on donkeys, riders on camels, he must be alert, fully alert.”
bsb.21:8: Then the lookout shouted: “Day after day, my lord, I stand on the watchtower; night after night I stay at my post.
bsb.21:9: Look, here come the riders, horsemen in pairs.” And one answered, saying: “Fallen, fallen is Babylon! All the images of her gods lie shattered on the ground!”
bsb.21:10: O my people, crushed on the threshing floor, I tell you what I have heard from the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel.
bsb.21:11: This is the burden against Dumah: One calls to me from Seir, “Watchman, what is left of the night? Watchman, what is left of the night?”
bsb.21:12: The watchman replies, “Morning has come, but also the night. If you would inquire, then inquire. Come back yet again.”
bsb.21:13: This is the burden against Arabia: In the thickets of Arabia you must lodge, O caravans of Dedanites.
bsb.21:14: Bring water for the thirsty, O dwellers of Tema; meet the refugees with food.
bsb.21:15: For they flee from the sword— the sword that is drawn— from the bow that is bent, and from the stress of battle.
bsb.21:16: For this is what the Lord says to me: “Within one year, as a hired worker would count it, all the glory of Kedar will be gone.
bsb.21:17: The remaining archers, the warriors of Kedar, will be few.” For the LORD, the God of Israel, has spoken.
bsb.22:1: This is the burden against the Valley of Vision: What ails you now, that you have all gone up to the rooftops,
bsb.22:2: O city of commotion, O town of revelry? Your slain did not die by the sword, nor were they killed in battle.
bsb.22:3: All your rulers have fled together, captured without a bow. All your fugitives were captured together, having fled to a distant place.
bsb.22:4: Therefore I said, “Turn away from me, let me weep bitterly! Do not try to console me over the destruction of the daughter of my people.”
bsb.22:5: For the Lord GOD of Hosts has set a day of tumult and trampling and confusion in the Valley of Vision— of breaking down the walls and crying to the mountains.
bsb.22:6: Elam takes up a quiver, with chariots and horsemen, and Kir uncovers the shield.
bsb.22:7: Your choicest valleys are full of chariots, and horsemen are posted at the gates.
bsb.22:8: He has uncovered the defenses of Judah. On that day you looked to the weapons in the House of the Forest.
bsb.22:9: You saw that there were many breaches in the walls of the City of David. You collected water from the lower pool.
bsb.22:10: You counted the houses of Jerusalem and tore them down to strengthen the wall.
bsb.22:11: You built a reservoir between the walls for the waters of the ancient pool, but you did not look to the One who made it, or consider Him who planned it long ago.
bsb.22:12: On that day the Lord GOD of Hosts called for weeping and wailing, for shaven heads and the wearing of sackcloth.
bsb.22:13: But look, there is joy and gladness, butchering of cattle and slaughtering of sheep, eating of meat and drinking of wine: “Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die!”
bsb.22:14: The LORD of Hosts has revealed in my hearing: “Until your dying day, this sin of yours will never be atoned for,” says the Lord GOD of Hosts.
bsb.22:15: This is what the Lord GOD of Hosts says: “Go, say to Shebna, the steward in charge of the palace:
bsb.22:16: What are you doing here, and who authorized you to carve out a tomb for yourself here—to chisel your tomb in the height and cut your resting place in the rock?
bsb.22:17: Look, O mighty man! The LORD is about to shake you violently. He will take hold of you,
bsb.22:18: roll you into a ball, and sling you into a wide land. There you will die, and there your glorious chariots will remain—a disgrace to the house of your master.
bsb.22:19: I will remove you from office, and you will be ousted from your position.
bsb.22:20: On that day I will summon My servant, Eliakim son of Hilkiah.
bsb.22:21: I will clothe him with your robe and tie your sash around him. I will put your authority in his hand, and he will be a father to the dwellers of Jerusalem and to the house of Judah.
bsb.22:22: I will place on his shoulder the key to the house of David. What he opens no one can shut, and what he shuts no one can open.
bsb.22:23: I will drive him like a peg into a firm place, and he will be a throne of glory for the house of his father.
bsb.22:24: So they will hang on him all the glory of his father’s house: the descendants and the offshoots—all the lesser vessels, from bowls to every kind of jar.
bsb.22:25: In that day, declares the LORD of Hosts, the peg driven into a firm place will give way; it will be sheared off and fall, and the load upon it will be cut down.” Indeed, the LORD has spoken.
bsb.23:1: This is the burden against Tyre: Wail, O ships of Tarshish, for Tyre is laid waste, without house or harbor. Word has reached them from the land of Cyprus.
bsb.23:2: Be silent, O dwellers of the coastland, you merchants of Sidon, whose traders have crossed the sea.
bsb.23:3: On the great waters came the grain of Shihor; the harvest of the Nile was the revenue of Tyre; she was the merchant of the nations.
bsb.23:4: Be ashamed, O Sidon, the stronghold of the sea, for the sea has spoken: “I have not been in labor or given birth. I have not raised young men or brought up young women.”
bsb.23:5: When the report reaches Egypt, they will writhe in agony over the news of Tyre.
bsb.23:6: Cross over to Tarshish; wail, O inhabitants of the coastland!
bsb.23:7: Is this your jubilant city, whose origin is from antiquity, whose feet have taken her to settle far away?
bsb.23:8: Who planned this against Tyre, the bestower of crowns, whose traders are princes, whose merchants are renowned on the earth?
bsb.23:9: The LORD of Hosts planned it, to defile all its glorious beauty, to disgrace all the renowned of the earth.
bsb.23:10: Cultivate your land like the Nile, O Daughter of Tarshish; there is no longer a harbor.
bsb.23:11: The LORD has stretched out His hand over the sea; He has made kingdoms tremble. He has given a command that the strongholds of Canaan be destroyed.
bsb.23:12: He said, “You shall rejoice no more, O oppressed Virgin Daughter of Sidon. Get up and cross over to Cyprus— even there you will find no rest.”
bsb.23:13: Look at the land of the Chaldeans— a people now of no account. The Assyrians destined it for the desert creatures; they set up their siege towers and stripped its palaces. They brought it to ruin.
bsb.23:14: Wail, O ships of Tarshish, for your harbor has been destroyed!
bsb.23:15: At that time Tyre will be forgotten for seventy years—the span of a king’s life. But at the end of seventy years, it will happen to Tyre as in the song of the harlot:
bsb.23:16: “Take up your harp, stroll through the city, O forgotten harlot. Make sweet melody, sing many a song, so you will be remembered.”
bsb.23:17: And at the end of seventy years, the LORD will restore Tyre. Then she will return to hire as a prostitute and sell herself to all the kingdoms on the face of the earth.
bsb.23:18: Yet her profits and wages will be set apart to the LORD; they will not be stored or saved, for her profit will go to those who live before the LORD, for abundant food and fine clothing.
bsb.24:1: Behold, the LORD lays waste the earth and leaves it in ruins. He will twist its surface and scatter its inhabitants—
bsb.24:2: people and priest alike, servant and master, maid and mistress, buyer and seller, lender and borrower, creditor and debtor.
bsb.24:3: The earth will be utterly laid waste and thoroughly plundered. For the LORD has spoken this word.
bsb.24:4: The earth mourns and withers; the world languishes and fades; the exalted of the earth waste away.
bsb.24:5: The earth is defiled by its people; they have transgressed the laws; they have overstepped the decrees and broken the everlasting covenant.
bsb.24:6: Therefore a curse has consumed the earth, and its inhabitants must bear the guilt; the earth’s dwellers have been burned, and only a few survive.
bsb.24:7: The new wine dries up, the vine withers. All the merrymakers now groan.
bsb.24:8: The joyful tambourines have ceased; the noise of revelers has stopped; the joyful harp is silent.
bsb.24:9: They no longer sing and drink wine; strong drink is bitter to those who consume it.
bsb.24:10: The city of chaos is shattered; every house is closed to entry.
bsb.24:11: In the streets they cry out for wine. All joy turns to gloom; rejoicing is exiled from the land.
bsb.24:12: The city is left in ruins; its gate is reduced to rubble.
bsb.24:13: So will it be on the earth and among the nations, like a harvested olive tree, like a gleaning after a grape harvest.
bsb.24:14: They raise their voices, they shout for joy; from the west they proclaim the majesty of the LORD.
bsb.24:15: Therefore glorify the LORD in the east. Extol the name of the LORD, the God of Israel in the islands of the sea.
bsb.24:16: From the ends of the earth we hear singing: “Glory to the Righteous One.” But I said, “I am wasting away! I am wasting away! Woe is me.” The treacherous betray; the treacherous deal in treachery.
bsb.24:17: Terror and pit and snare await you, O dweller of the earth.
bsb.24:18: Whoever flees the sound of panic will fall into the pit, and whoever climbs from the pit will be caught in the snare. For the windows of heaven are open, and the foundations of the earth are shaken.
bsb.24:19: The earth is utterly broken apart, the earth is split open, the earth is shaken violently.
bsb.24:20: The earth staggers like a drunkard and sways like a shack. Earth’s rebellion weighs it down, and it falls, never to rise again.
bsb.24:21: In that day the LORD will punish the host of heaven above and the kings of the earth below.
bsb.24:22: They will be gathered together like prisoners in a pit. They will be confined to a dungeon and punished after many days.
bsb.24:23: The moon will be confounded and the sun will be ashamed; for the LORD of Hosts will reign on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, and before His elders with great glory.
bsb.25:1: O LORD, You are my God! I will exalt You; I will praise Your name. For You have worked wonders— plans formed long ago— in perfect faithfulness.
bsb.25:2: Indeed, You have made the city a heap of rubble, the fortified town a ruin. The fortress of strangers is a city no more; it will never be rebuilt.
bsb.25:3: Therefore, a strong people will honor You. The cities of ruthless nations will revere You.
bsb.25:4: For You have been a refuge for the poor, a stronghold for the needy in distress, a refuge from the storm, a shade from the heat. For the breath of the ruthless is like rain against a wall,
bsb.25:5: like heat in a dry land. You subdue the uproar of foreigners. As the shade of a cloud cools the heat, so the song of the ruthless is silenced.
bsb.25:6: On this mountain the LORD of Hosts will prepare a banquet for all the peoples, a feast of aged wine, of choice meat, of finely aged wine.
bsb.25:7: On this mountain He will swallow up the shroud that enfolds all peoples, the sheet that covers all nations;
bsb.25:8: He will swallow up death forever. The Lord GOD will wipe away the tears from every face and remove the disgrace of His people from the whole earth. For the LORD has spoken.
bsb.25:9: And in that day it will be said, “Surely this is our God; we have waited for Him, and He has saved us. This is the LORD for whom we have waited. Let us rejoice and be glad in His salvation.”
bsb.25:10: For the hand of the LORD will rest on this mountain. But Moab will be trampled in his place as straw is trodden into the dung pile.
bsb.25:11: He will spread out his hands within it, as a swimmer spreads his arms to swim. His pride will be brought low, despite the skill of his hands.
bsb.25:12: The high-walled fortress will be brought down, cast to the ground, into the dust.
bsb.26:1: In that day this song will be sung in the land of Judah: We have a strong city; salvation is established as its walls and ramparts.
bsb.26:2: Open the gates so a righteous nation may enter— one that remains faithful.
bsb.26:3: You will keep in perfect peace the steadfast of mind, because he trusts in You.
bsb.26:4: Trust in the LORD forever, because GOD the LORD is the Rock eternal.
bsb.26:5: For He has humbled those who dwell on high; He lays the lofty city low. He brings it down to the ground; He casts it into the dust.
bsb.26:6: Feet trample it down— the feet of the oppressed, the steps of the poor.
bsb.26:7: The path of the righteous is level; You clear a straight path for the upright.
bsb.26:8: Yes, we wait for You, O LORD; we walk in the path of Your judgments. Your name and renown are the desire of our souls.
bsb.26:9: My soul longs for You in the night; indeed, my spirit seeks You at dawn. For when Your judgments come upon the earth, the people of the world learn righteousness.
bsb.26:10: Though grace is shown to the wicked man, he does not learn righteousness. In the land of righteousness he acts unjustly and fails to see the majesty of the LORD.
bsb.26:11: O LORD, Your hand is upraised, but they do not see it. They will see Your zeal for Your people and be put to shame. The fire set for Your enemies will consume them!
bsb.26:12: O LORD, You will establish peace for us. For all that we have accomplished, You have done for us.
bsb.26:13: O LORD our God, other lords besides You have had dominion, but Your name alone do we confess.
bsb.26:14: The dead will not live; the departed spirits will not rise. Therefore You have punished and destroyed them; You have wiped out all memory of them.
bsb.26:15: You have enlarged the nation, O LORD; You have enlarged the nation. You have gained glory for Yourself; You have extended all the borders of the land.
bsb.26:16: O LORD, they sought You in their distress; when You disciplined them, they poured out a quiet prayer.
bsb.26:17: As a woman with child about to give birth writhes and cries out in pain, so were we in Your presence, O LORD.
bsb.26:18: We were with child; we writhed in pain; but we gave birth to wind. We have given no salvation to the earth, nor brought any life into the world.
bsb.26:19: Your dead will live; their bodies will rise. Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust! For your dew is like the dew of the morning, and the earth will bring forth her dead.
bsb.26:20: Go, my people, enter your rooms and shut your doors behind you. Hide yourselves a little while until the wrath has passed.
bsb.26:21: For behold, the LORD is coming out of His dwelling to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity. The earth will reveal her bloodshed and will no longer conceal her slain.
bsb.27:1: In that day the LORD will take His sharp, great, and mighty sword, and bring judgment on Leviathan the fleeing serpent—Leviathan the coiling serpent—and He will slay the dragon of the sea.
bsb.27:2: In that day: “Sing about a fruitful vineyard.
bsb.27:3: I, the LORD, am its keeper; I water it continually. I guard it night and day so no one can disturb it;
bsb.27:4: I am not angry. If only thorns and briers confronted Me, I would march and trample them, I would burn them to the ground.
bsb.27:5: Or let them lay claim to My protection; let them make peace with Me— yes, let them make peace with Me.”
bsb.27:6: In the days to come, Jacob will take root. Israel will bud and blossom and fill the whole world with fruit.
bsb.27:7: Has the LORD struck Israel as He struck her oppressors? Was she killed like those who slayed her?
bsb.27:8: By warfare and exile You contended with her and removed her with a fierce wind, as on the day the east wind blows.
bsb.27:9: Therefore Jacob’s guilt will be atoned for, and the full fruit of the removal of his sin will be this: When he makes all the altar stones like crushed bits of chalk, no Asherah poles or incense altars will remain standing.
bsb.27:10: For the fortified city lies deserted— a homestead abandoned, a wilderness forsaken. There the calves graze, and there they lie down; they strip its branches bare.
bsb.27:11: When its limbs are dry, they are broken off. Women come and use them for kindling; for this is a people without understanding. Therefore their Maker has no compassion on them, and their Creator shows them no favor.
bsb.27:12: In that day the LORD will thresh from the flowing Euphrates to the Wadi of Egypt, and you, O Israelites, will be gathered one by one.
bsb.27:13: And in that day a great ram’s horn will sound, and those who were perishing in Assyria will come forth with those who were exiles in Egypt. And they will worship the LORD on the holy mountain in Jerusalem.
bsb.28:1: Woe to the majestic crown of Ephraim’s drunkards, to the fading flower of his glorious splendor, set on the summit above the fertile valley, the pride of those overcome by wine.
bsb.28:2: Behold, the Lord has one who is strong and mighty. Like a hailstorm or destructive tempest, like a driving rain or flooding downpour, he will smash that crown to the ground.
bsb.28:3: The majestic crown of Ephraim’s drunkards will be trampled underfoot.
bsb.28:4: The fading flower of his beautiful splendor, set on the summit above the fertile valley, will be like a ripe fig before the summer harvest: Whoever sees it will take it in his hand and swallow it.
bsb.28:5: On that day the LORD of Hosts will be a crown of glory, a diadem of splendor to the remnant of His people,
bsb.28:6: a spirit of justice to him who sits in judgment, and a strength to those who repel the onslaught at the gate.
bsb.28:7: These also stagger from wine and stumble from strong drink: Priests and prophets reel from strong drink and are befuddled by wine. They stumble because of strong drink, muddled in their visions and stumbling in their judgments.
bsb.28:8: For all their tables are covered with vomit; there is not a place without filth.
bsb.28:9: Whom is He trying to teach? To whom is He explaining His message? To infants just weaned from milk? To babies removed from the breast?
bsb.28:10: For they hear: “Order on order, order on order, line on line, line on line; a little here, a little there.”
bsb.28:11: Indeed, with mocking lips and foreign tongues, He will speak to this people
bsb.28:12: to whom He has said: “This is the place of rest, let the weary rest; this is the place of repose.” But they would not listen.
bsb.28:13: Then the word of the LORD to them will become: “Order on order, order on order, line on line, line on line; a little here, a little there,” so that they will go stumbling backward and will be injured, ensnared, and captured.
bsb.28:14: Therefore hear the word of the LORD, O scoffers who rule this people in Jerusalem.
bsb.28:15: For you said, “We have made a covenant with death; we have fashioned an agreement with Sheol. When the overwhelming scourge passes through it will not touch us, because we have made lies our refuge and falsehood our hiding place.”
bsb.28:16: So this is what the Lord GOD says: “See, I lay a stone in Zion, a tested stone, a precious cornerstone, a sure foundation; the one who believes will never be shaken.
bsb.28:17: I will make justice the measuring line and righteousness the level. Hail will sweep away your refuge of lies, and water will flood your hiding place.
bsb.28:18: Your covenant with death will be dissolved, and your agreement with Sheol will not stand. When the overwhelming scourge passes through, you will be trampled by it.
bsb.28:19: As often as it passes through, it will carry you away; it will sweep through morning after morning, by day and by night.” The understanding of this message will bring sheer terror.
bsb.28:20: Indeed, the bed is too short to stretch out on, and the blanket too small to wrap around you.
bsb.28:21: For the LORD will rise up as at Mount Perazim. He will rouse Himself as in the Valley of Gibeon, to do His work, His strange work, and to perform His task, His disturbing task.
bsb.28:22: So now, do not mock, or your shackles will become heavier. Indeed, I have heard from the Lord GOD of Hosts a decree of destruction against the whole land.
bsb.28:23: Listen and hear my voice. Pay attention and hear what I say.
bsb.28:24: Does the plowman plow for planting every day? Does he continuously loosen and harrow the soil?
bsb.28:25: When he has leveled its surface, does he not sow caraway and scatter cumin? He plants wheat in rows and barley in plots, and rye within its border.
bsb.28:26: For his God instructs and teaches him properly.
bsb.28:27: Surely caraway is not threshed with a sledge, and the wheel of a cart is not rolled over the cumin. But caraway is beaten out with a stick, and cumin with a rod.
bsb.28:28: Grain for bread must be ground, but it is not endlessly threshed. Though the wheels of the cart roll over it, the horses do not crush it.
bsb.28:29: This also comes from the LORD of Hosts, who is wonderful in counsel and excellent in wisdom.
bsb.29:1: Woe to you, O Ariel, the city of Ariel where David camped! Year upon year let your festivals recur.
bsb.29:2: And I will constrain Ariel, and there will be mourning and lamentation; she will be like an altar hearth before Me.
bsb.29:3: I will camp in a circle around you; I will besiege you with towers and set up siege works against you.
bsb.29:4: You will be brought low, you will speak from the ground, and out of the dust your words will be muffled. Your voice will be like a spirit from the ground; your speech will whisper out of the dust.
bsb.29:5: But your many foes will be like fine dust, the multitude of the ruthless like blowing chaff. Then suddenly, in an instant,
bsb.29:6: you will be visited by the LORD of Hosts with thunder and earthquake and loud noise, with windstorm and tempest and consuming flame of fire.
bsb.29:7: All the many nations going out to battle against Ariel— even all who war against her, laying siege and attacking her— will be like a dream, like a vision in the night,
bsb.29:8: as when a hungry man dreams he is eating, then awakens still hungry; as when a thirsty man dreams he is drinking, then awakens faint and parched. So will it be for all the many nations who go to battle against Mount Zion.
bsb.29:9: Stop and be astonished; blind yourselves and be sightless; be drunk, but not with wine; stagger, but not from strong drink.
bsb.29:10: For the LORD has poured out on you a spirit of deep sleep. He has shut your eyes, O prophets; He has covered your heads, O seers.
bsb.29:11: And the entire vision will be to you like the words sealed in a scroll. If it is handed to someone to read, he will say, “I cannot, because it is sealed.”
bsb.29:12: Or if the scroll is handed to one unable to read, he will say, “I cannot read.”
bsb.29:13: Therefore the Lord said: “These people draw near to Me with their mouths and honor Me with their lips, but their hearts are far from Me. Their worship of Me is but rules taught by men.
bsb.29:14: Therefore I will again confound these people with wonder upon wonder. The wisdom of the wise will vanish, and the intelligence of the intelligent will be hidden.”
bsb.29:15: Woe to those who dig deep to hide their plans from the LORD. In darkness they do their works and say, “Who sees us, and who will know?”
bsb.29:16: You have turned things upside down, as if the potter were regarded as clay. Shall what is formed say to him who formed it, “He did not make me”? Can the pottery say of the potter, “He has no understanding”?
bsb.29:17: In a very short time, will not Lebanon become an orchard, and the orchard seem like a forest?
bsb.29:18: On that day the deaf will hear the words of the scroll, and out of the deep darkness the eyes of the blind will see.
bsb.29:19: The humble will increase their joy in the LORD, and the poor among men will rejoice in the Holy One of Israel.
bsb.29:20: For the ruthless will vanish, the mockers will disappear, and all who look for evil will be cut down—
bsb.29:21: those who indict a man with a word, who ensnare the mediator at the gate, and who with false charges deprive the innocent of justice.
bsb.29:22: Therefore the LORD who redeemed Abraham says of the house of Jacob: “No longer will Jacob be ashamed and no more will his face grow pale.
bsb.29:23: For when he sees his children around him, the work of My hands, they will honor My name, they will sanctify the Holy One of Jacob, and they will stand in awe of the God of Israel.
bsb.29:24: Then the wayward in spirit will come to understanding, and those who grumble will accept instruction.”
bsb.30:1: “Woe to the rebellious children,” declares the LORD, “to those who carry out a plan that is not Mine, who form an alliance, but against My will, heaping up sin upon sin.
bsb.30:2: They set out to go down to Egypt without asking My advice, to seek shelter under Pharaoh’s protection and take refuge in Egypt’s shade.
bsb.30:3: But Pharaoh’s protection will become your shame, and the refuge of Egypt’s shade your disgrace.
bsb.30:4: For though their princes are at Zoan and their envoys have arrived in Hanes,
bsb.30:5: everyone will be put to shame because of a people useless to them. They cannot be of help; they are good for nothing but shame and reproach.”
bsb.30:6: This is the burden against the beasts of the Negev: Through a land of hardship and distress, of lioness and lion, of viper and flying serpent, they carry their wealth on the backs of donkeys and their treasures on the humps of camels, to a people of no profit to them.
bsb.30:7: Egypt’s help is futile and empty; therefore I have called her Rahab Who Sits Still.
bsb.30:8: Go now, write it on a tablet in their presence and inscribe it on a scroll; it will be for the days to come, a witness forever and ever.
bsb.30:9: These are rebellious people, deceitful children, children unwilling to obey the LORD’s instruction.
bsb.30:10: They say to the seers, “Stop seeing visions!” and to the prophets, “Do not prophesy to us the truth! Speak to us pleasant words; prophesy illusions.
bsb.30:11: Get out of the way; turn off the road. Rid us of the Holy One of Israel!”
bsb.30:12: Therefore this is what the Holy One of Israel says: “Because you have rejected this message, trusting in oppression and relying on deceit,
bsb.30:13: this iniquity of yours is like a breach about to fail, a bulge in a high wall, whose collapse will come suddenly— in an instant!
bsb.30:14: It will break in pieces like a potter’s jar, shattered so that no fragment can be found. Not a shard will be found in the dust large enough to scoop the coals from a hearth or to skim the water from a cistern.”
bsb.30:15: For the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel, has said: “By repentance and rest you would be saved; your strength would lie in quiet confidence— but you were not willing.”
bsb.30:16: “No,” you say, “we will flee on horses.” Therefore you will flee! “We will ride swift horses,” but your pursuers will be faster.
bsb.30:17: A thousand will flee at the threat of one; at the threat of five you will all flee, until you are left alone like a pole on a mountaintop, like a banner on a hill.
bsb.30:18: Therefore the LORD longs to be gracious to you; therefore He rises to show you compassion, for the LORD is a just God. Blessed are all who wait for Him.
bsb.30:19: O people in Zion who dwell in Jerusalem, you will weep no more. He will surely be gracious when you cry for help; when He hears, He will answer you.
bsb.30:20: The Lord will give you the bread of adversity and the water of affliction, but your Teacher will no longer hide Himself—with your own eyes you will see Him.
bsb.30:21: And whether you turn to the right or to the left, your ears will hear this command behind you: “This is the way. Walk in it.”
bsb.30:22: So you will desecrate your silver-plated idols and your gold-plated images. You will throw them away like menstrual cloths, saying to them, “Be gone!”
bsb.30:23: Then He will send rain for the seed that you have sown in the ground, and the food that comes from your land will be rich and plentiful. On that day your cattle will graze in open pastures.
bsb.30:24: The oxen and donkeys that work the ground will eat salted fodder, winnowed with shovel and pitchfork.
bsb.30:25: And from every high mountain and every raised hill, streams of water will flow in the day of great slaughter, when the towers fall.
bsb.30:26: The light of the moon will be as bright as the sun, and the light of the sun will be seven times brighter—like the light of seven days—on the day that the LORD binds up the brokenness of His people and heals the wounds He has inflicted.
bsb.30:27: Behold, the Name of the LORD comes from afar, with burning anger and dense smoke. His lips are full of fury, and His tongue is like a consuming fire.
bsb.30:28: His breath is like a rushing torrent that rises to the neck. He comes to sift the nations in a sieve of destruction; He bridles the jaws of the peoples to lead them astray.
bsb.30:29: You will sing as on the night of a holy festival, and your heart will rejoice like one who walks to the music of a flute, going up to the mountain of the LORD, to the Rock of Israel.
bsb.30:30: And the LORD will cause His majestic voice to be heard and His mighty arm to be revealed, striking in angry wrath with a flame of consuming fire, and with cloudburst, storm, and hailstones.
bsb.30:31: For Assyria will be shattered at the voice of the LORD; He will strike them with His scepter.
bsb.30:32: And with every stroke of the rod of punishment that the LORD brings down on them, the tambourines and lyres will sound as He battles with weapons brandished.
bsb.30:33: For Topheth has long been prepared; it has been made ready for the king. Its funeral pyre is deep and wide, with plenty of fire and wood. The breath of the LORD, like a torrent of burning sulfur, sets it ablaze.
bsb.31:1: Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help, who rely on horses, who trust in their abundance of chariots and in their multitude of horsemen. They do not look to the Holy One of Israel; they do not seek the LORD.
bsb.31:2: Yet He too is wise and brings disaster; He does not call back His words. He will rise up against the house of the wicked and against the allies of evildoers.
bsb.31:3: But the Egyptians are men, not God; their horses are flesh, not spirit. When the LORD stretches out His hand, the helper will stumble, and the one he helps will fall; both will perish together.
bsb.31:4: For this is what the LORD has said to me: “Like a lion roaring or a young lion over its prey— and though a band of shepherds is called out against it, it is not terrified by their shouting or subdued by their clamor— so the LORD of Hosts will come down to do battle on Mount Zion and its heights.
bsb.31:5: Like birds hovering overhead, so the LORD of Hosts will protect Jerusalem. He will shield it and deliver it; He will pass over it and preserve it.”
bsb.31:6: Return to the One against whom you have so blatantly rebelled, O children of Israel.
bsb.31:7: For on that day, every one of you will reject the idols of silver and gold that your own hands have sinfully made.
bsb.31:8: “Then Assyria will fall, but not by the sword of man; a sword will devour them, but not one made by mortals. They will flee before the sword, and their young men will be put to forced labor.
bsb.31:9: Their rock will pass away for fear, and their princes will panic at the sight of the battle standard,” declares the LORD, whose fire is in Zion, whose furnace is in Jerusalem.
bsb.32:1: Behold, a king will reign in righteousness, and princes will rule with justice.
bsb.32:2: Each will be like a shelter from the wind, a refuge from the storm, like streams of water in a dry land, like the shadow of a great rock in an arid land.
bsb.32:3: Then the eyes of those who see will no longer be closed, and the ears of those who hear will listen.
bsb.32:4: The mind of the rash will know and understand, and the stammering tongue will speak clearly and fluently.
bsb.32:5: No longer will a fool be called noble, nor a scoundrel be respected.
bsb.32:6: For a fool speaks foolishness; his mind plots iniquity. He practices ungodliness and speaks falsely about the LORD; he leaves the hungry empty and deprives the thirsty of drink.
bsb.32:7: The weapons of the scoundrel are destructive; he hatches plots to destroy the poor with lies, even when the plea of the needy is just.
bsb.32:8: But a noble man makes honorable plans; he stands up for worthy causes.
bsb.32:9: Stand up, you complacent women; listen to me. Give ear to my word, you overconfident daughters.
bsb.32:10: In a little more than a year you will tremble, O secure ones. For the grape harvest will fail and the fruit harvest will not arrive.
bsb.32:11: Shudder, you ladies of leisure; tremble, you daughters of complacency. Strip yourselves bare and put sackcloth around your waists.
bsb.32:12: Beat your breasts for the pleasant fields, for the fruitful vines,
bsb.32:13: and for the land of my people, overgrown with thorns and briers— even for every house of merriment in this city of revelry.
bsb.32:14: For the palace will be forsaken, the busy city abandoned. The hill and the watchtower will become caves forever— the delight of wild donkeys and a pasture for flocks—
bsb.32:15: until the Spirit is poured out upon us from on high. Then the desert will be an orchard, and the orchard will seem like a forest.
bsb.32:16: Then justice will inhabit the wilderness, and righteousness will dwell in the fertile field.
bsb.32:17: The work of righteousness will be peace; the service of righteousness will be quiet confidence forever.
bsb.32:18: Then my people will dwell in a peaceful place, in safe and secure places of rest.
bsb.32:19: But hail will level the forest, and the city will sink to the depths.
bsb.32:20: Blessed are those who sow beside abundant waters, who let the ox and donkey range freely.
bsb.33:1: Woe to you, O destroyer never destroyed, O traitor never betrayed! When you have finished destroying, you will be destroyed. When you have finished betraying, you will be betrayed.
bsb.33:2: O LORD, be gracious to us! We wait for You. Be our strength every morning and our salvation in time of trouble.
bsb.33:3: The peoples flee the thunder of Your voice; the nations scatter when You rise.
bsb.33:4: Your spoil, O nations, is gathered as by locusts; like a swarm of locusts men sweep over it.
bsb.33:5: The LORD is exalted, for He dwells on high; He has filled Zion with justice and righteousness.
bsb.33:6: He will be the sure foundation for your times, a storehouse of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge. The fear of the LORD is Zion’s treasure.
bsb.33:7: Behold, their valiant ones cry aloud in the streets; the envoys of peace weep bitterly.
bsb.33:8: The highways are deserted; travel has ceased. The treaty has been broken, the witnesses are despised, and human life is disregarded.
bsb.33:9: The land mourns and languishes; Lebanon is ashamed and decayed. Sharon is like a desert; Bashan and Carmel shake off their leaves.
bsb.33:10: “Now I will arise,” says the LORD. “Now I will lift Myself up. Now I will be exalted.
bsb.33:11: You conceive chaff; you give birth to stubble. Your breath is a fire that will consume you.
bsb.33:12: The peoples will be burned to ashes, like thorns cut down and set ablaze.
bsb.33:13: You who are far off, hear what I have done; you who are near, acknowledge My might.”
bsb.33:14: The sinners in Zion are afraid; trembling grips the ungodly: “Who of us can dwell with a consuming fire? Who of us can dwell with everlasting flames?”
bsb.33:15: He who walks righteously and speaks with sincerity, who refuses gain from extortion, whose hand never takes a bribe, who stops his ears against murderous plots and shuts his eyes tightly against evil—
bsb.33:16: he will dwell on the heights; the mountain fortress will be his refuge; his food will be provided and his water assured.
bsb.33:17: Your eyes will see the King in His beauty and behold a land that stretches afar.
bsb.33:18: Your mind will ponder the former terror: “Where is he who tallies? Where is he who weighs? Where is he who counts the towers?”
bsb.33:19: You will no longer see the insolent, a people whose speech is unintelligible, who stammer in a language you cannot understand.
bsb.33:20: Look upon Zion, the city of our appointed feasts. Your eyes will see Jerusalem, a peaceful pasture, a tent that does not wander; its tent pegs will not be pulled up, nor will any of its cords be broken.
bsb.33:21: But there the Majestic One, our LORD, will be for us a place of rivers and wide canals, where no galley with oars will row, and no majestic vessel will pass.
bsb.33:22: For the LORD is our Judge, the LORD is our lawgiver, the LORD is our King. It is He who will save us.
bsb.33:23: Your ropes are slack; they cannot secure the mast or spread the sail. Then an abundance of spoils will be divided, and even the lame will carry off plunder.
bsb.33:24: And no resident of Zion will say, “I am sick.” The people who dwell there will be forgiven of iniquity.
bsb.34:1: Come near, O nations, to listen; pay attention, O peoples. Let the earth hear, and all that fills it, the world and all that springs from it.
bsb.34:2: The LORD is angry with all the nations and furious with all their armies. He will devote them to destruction; He will give them over to slaughter.
bsb.34:3: Their slain will be left unburied, and the stench of their corpses will rise; the mountains will flow with their blood.
bsb.34:4: All the stars of heaven will be dissolved. The skies will be rolled up like a scroll, and all their stars will fall like withered leaves from the vine, like foliage from the fig tree.
bsb.34:5: When My sword has drunk its fill in the heavens, then it will come down upon Edom, upon the people I have devoted to destruction.
bsb.34:6: The sword of the LORD is bathed in blood. It drips with fat— with the blood of lambs and goats, with the fat of the kidneys of rams. For the LORD has a sacrifice in Bozrah, a great slaughter in the land of Edom.
bsb.34:7: And the wild oxen will fall with them, the young bulls with the strong ones. Their land will be drenched with blood, and their soil will be soaked with fat.
bsb.34:8: For the LORD has a day of vengeance, a year of recompense for the cause of Zion.
bsb.34:9: Edom’s streams will be turned to tar, and her soil to sulfur; her land will become a blazing pitch.
bsb.34:10: It will not be quenched—day or night. Its smoke will ascend forever. From generation to generation it will lie desolate; no one will ever again pass through it.
bsb.34:11: The desert owl and screech owl will possess it, and the great owl and raven will dwell in it. The LORD will stretch out over Edom a measuring line of chaos and a plumb line of destruction.
bsb.34:12: No nobles will be left to proclaim a king, and all her princes will come to nothing.
bsb.34:13: Her towers will be overgrown with thorns, her fortresses with thistles and briers. She will become a haunt for jackals, an abode for ostriches.
bsb.34:14: The desert creatures will meet with hyenas, and one wild goat will call to another. There the night creature will settle and find her place of repose.
bsb.34:15: There the owl will make her nest; she will lay and hatch her eggs and gather her brood under her shadow. Even there the birds of prey will gather, each with its mate.
bsb.34:16: Search and read the scroll of the LORD: Not one of these will go missing, not one will lack her mate, because He has ordered it by His mouth, and He will gather them by His Spirit.
bsb.34:17: He has allotted their portion; His hand has distributed it by measure. They will possess it forever; they will dwell in it from generation to generation.
bsb.35:1: The wilderness and the land will be glad; the desert will rejoice and blossom like a rose.
bsb.35:2: It will bloom profusely and rejoice with joy and singing. The glory of Lebanon will be given to it, the splendor of Carmel and Sharon. They will see the glory of the LORD, the splendor of our God.
bsb.35:3: Strengthen the limp hands and steady the feeble knees!
bsb.35:4: Say to those with anxious hearts: “Be strong, do not fear! Behold, your God will come with vengeance. With divine retribution He will come to save you.”
bsb.35:5: Then the eyes of the blind will be opened and the ears of the deaf unstopped.
bsb.35:6: Then the lame will leap like a deer and the mute tongue will shout for joy. For waters will gush forth in the wilderness, and streams in the desert.
bsb.35:7: The parched ground will become a pool, the thirsty land springs of water. In the haunt where jackals once lay, there will be grass and reeds and papyrus.
bsb.35:8: And there will be a highway called the Way of Holiness. The unclean will not travel it— only those who walk in the Way— and fools will not stray onto it.
bsb.35:9: No lion will be there, and no vicious beast will go up on it. Such will not be found there, but the redeemed will walk upon it.
bsb.35:10: So the redeemed of the LORD will return and enter Zion with singing, crowned with everlasting joy. Gladness and joy will overtake them, and sorrow and sighing will flee.
bsb.36:1: In the fourteenth year of Hezekiah’s reign, Sennacherib king of Assyria attacked and captured all the fortified cities of Judah.
bsb.36:2: And the king of Assyria sent the Rabshakeh, with a great army, from Lachish to King Hezekiah at Jerusalem. And he stopped by the aqueduct of the upper pool, on the road to the Launderer’s Field.
bsb.36:3: Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah the palace administrator, Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph the recorder, went out to him.
bsb.36:4: The Rabshakeh said to them, “Tell Hezekiah that this is what the great king, the king of Assyria, says: What is the basis of this confidence of yours?
bsb.36:5: You claim to have a strategy and strength for war, but these are empty words. In whom are you now trusting, that you have rebelled against me?
bsb.36:6: Look now, you are trusting in Egypt, that splintered reed of a staff that will pierce the hand of anyone who leans on it. Such is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who trust in him.
bsb.36:7: But if you say to me, ‘We trust in the LORD our God,’ is He not the One whose high places and altars Hezekiah has removed, saying to Judah and Jerusalem, ‘You must worship before this altar’?
bsb.36:8: Now, therefore, make a bargain with my master, the king of Assyria. I will give you two thousand horses—if you can put riders on them!
bsb.36:9: For how can you repel a single officer among the least of my master’s servants when you depend on Egypt for chariots and horsemen?
bsb.36:10: So now, was it apart from the LORD that I have come up against this land to destroy it? The LORD Himself said to me, ‘Go up against this land and destroy it.’”
bsb.36:11: Then Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said to the Rabshakeh, “Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, since we understand it. Do not speak to us in Hebrew in the hearing of the people on the wall.”
bsb.36:12: But the Rabshakeh replied, “Has my master sent me to speak these words only to you and your master, and not to the men sitting on the wall, who are destined with you to eat their own dung and drink their own urine?”
bsb.36:13: Then the Rabshakeh stood and called out loudly in Hebrew: “Hear the words of the great king, the king of Assyria!
bsb.36:14: This is what the king says: Do not let Hezekiah deceive you, for he cannot deliver you.
bsb.36:15: Do not let Hezekiah persuade you to trust in the LORD when he says, ‘The LORD will surely deliver us; this city will not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.’
bsb.36:16: Do not listen to Hezekiah, for this is what the king of Assyria says: Make peace with me and come out to me. Then every one of you will eat from his own vine and his own fig tree, and drink water from his own cistern,
bsb.36:17: until I come and take you away to a land like your own—a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards.
bsb.36:18: Do not let Hezekiah mislead you when he says, ‘The LORD will deliver us.’ Has the god of any nation ever delivered his land from the hand of the king of Assyria?
bsb.36:19: Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim? Have they delivered Samaria from my hand?
bsb.36:20: Who among all the gods of these lands has delivered his land from my hand? How then can the LORD deliver Jerusalem from my hand?”
bsb.36:21: But the people remained silent and did not answer a word, for Hezekiah had commanded, “Do not answer him.”
bsb.36:22: Then Hilkiah’s son Eliakim the palace administrator, Shebna the scribe, and Asaph’s son Joah the recorder came to Hezekiah with their clothes torn, and they relayed to him the words of the Rabshakeh.
bsb.37:1: On hearing this report, King Hezekiah tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and entered the house of the LORD.
bsb.37:2: And he sent Eliakim the palace administrator, Shebna the scribe, and the leading priests, all wearing sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz
bsb.37:3: to tell him, “This is what Hezekiah says: Today is a day of distress, rebuke, and disgrace; for children have come to the point of birth, but there is no strength to deliver them.
bsb.37:4: Perhaps the LORD your God will hear the words of the Rabshakeh, whom his master the king of Assyria has sent to defy the living God, and He will rebuke him for the words that the LORD your God has heard. Therefore lift up a prayer for the remnant that still survives.”
bsb.37:5: So the servants of King Hezekiah went to Isaiah,
bsb.37:6: who replied, “Tell your master that this is what the LORD says: ‘Do not be afraid of the words you have heard, with which the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed Me.
bsb.37:7: Behold, I will put a spirit in him so that he will hear a rumor and return to his own land, where I will cause him to fall by the sword.’”
bsb.37:8: When the Rabshakeh heard that the king of Assyria had left Lachish, he withdrew and found the king fighting against Libnah.
bsb.37:9: Now Sennacherib had been warned about Tirhakah king of Cush: “He has set out to fight against you.” On hearing this, Sennacherib sent messengers to Hezekiah, saying,
bsb.37:10: “Give this message to Hezekiah king of Judah: ‘Do not let your God, in whom you trust, deceive you by saying that Jerusalem will not be delivered into the hand of the king of Assyria.
bsb.37:11: Surely you have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the other countries, devoting them to destruction. Will you then be spared?
bsb.37:12: Did the gods of the nations destroyed by my fathers rescue those nations—the gods of Gozan, Haran, and Rezeph, and of the people of Eden in Telassar?
bsb.37:13: Where are the kings of Hamath, Arpad, Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah?’”
bsb.37:14: So Hezekiah received the letter from the messengers, read it, and went up to the house of the LORD and spread it out before the LORD.
bsb.37:15: And Hezekiah prayed to the LORD:
bsb.37:16: “O LORD of Hosts, God of Israel, enthroned above the cherubim, You alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth. You made the heavens and the earth.
bsb.37:17: Incline Your ear, O LORD, and hear; open Your eyes, O LORD, and see. Listen to all the words that Sennacherib has sent to defy the living God.
bsb.37:18: Truly, O LORD, the kings of Assyria have laid waste all these countries and their lands.
bsb.37:19: They have cast their gods into the fire and destroyed them, for they were not gods, but only wood and stone—the work of human hands.
bsb.37:20: And now, O LORD our God, save us from his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that You alone, O LORD, are God.”
bsb.37:21: Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent a message to Hezekiah: “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Because you have prayed to Me concerning Sennacherib king of Assyria,
bsb.37:22: this is the word that the LORD has spoken against him: ‘The Virgin Daughter of Zion despises you and mocks you; the Daughter of Jerusalem shakes her head behind you.
bsb.37:23: Whom have you taunted and blasphemed? Against whom have you raised your voice and lifted your eyes in pride? Against the Holy One of Israel!
bsb.37:24: Through your servants you have taunted the Lord, and you have said: “With my many chariots I have ascended to the heights of the mountains, to the remote peaks of Lebanon. I have cut down its tallest cedars, the finest of its cypresses. I have reached its farthest heights, the densest of its forests.
bsb.37:25: I have dug wells and drunk foreign waters. With the soles of my feet I have dried up all the streams of Egypt.”
bsb.37:26: Have you not heard? Long ago I ordained it; in days of old I planned it. Now I have brought it to pass, that you should crush fortified cities into piles of rubble.
bsb.37:27: Therefore their inhabitants, devoid of power, are dismayed and ashamed. They are like plants in the field, tender green shoots, grass on the rooftops, scorched before it is grown.
bsb.37:28: But I know your sitting down, your going out and coming in, and your raging against Me.
bsb.37:29: Because your rage and arrogance against Me have reached My ears, I will put My hook in your nose and My bit in your mouth; I will send you back the way you came.’
bsb.37:30: And this will be a sign to you, O Hezekiah: This year you will eat what grows on its own, and in the second year what springs from the same. But in the third year you will sow and reap; you will plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
bsb.37:31: And the surviving remnant of the house of Judah will again take root below and bear fruit above.
bsb.37:32: For a remnant will go forth from Jerusalem, and survivors from Mount Zion. The zeal of the LORD of Hosts will accomplish this.
bsb.37:33: So this is what the LORD says about the king of Assyria: ‘He will not enter this city or shoot an arrow into it. He will not come before it with a shield or build up a siege ramp against it.
bsb.37:34: He will go back the way he came, and he will not enter this city,’ declares the LORD.
bsb.37:35: ‘I will defend this city and save it for My own sake and for the sake of My servant David.’”
bsb.37:36: Then the angel of the LORD went out and struck down 185,000 men in the camp of the Assyrians. When the people got up the next morning, there were all the dead bodies!
bsb.37:37: So Sennacherib king of Assyria broke camp and withdrew. He returned to Nineveh and stayed there.
bsb.37:38: One day, while he was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer put him to the sword and escaped to the land of Ararat. And his son Esar-haddon reigned in his place.
bsb.38:1: In those days Hezekiah became mortally ill. The prophet Isaiah son of Amoz came to him and said, “This is what the LORD says: ‘Put your house in order, for you are about to die; you will not recover.’”
bsb.38:2: Then Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD,
bsb.38:3: saying, “Please, O LORD, remember how I have walked before You faithfully and with wholehearted devotion; I have done what was good in Your sight.” And Hezekiah wept bitterly.
bsb.38:4: And the word of the LORD came to Isaiah, saying,
bsb.38:5: “Go and tell Hezekiah that this is what the LORD, the God of your father David, says: ‘I have heard your prayer; I have seen your tears. Behold, I will add fifteen years to your life.
bsb.38:6: And I will deliver you and this city from the hand of the king of Assyria. I will defend this city.
bsb.38:7: This will be a sign to you from the LORD that He will do what He has promised:
bsb.38:8: I will make the sun’s shadow that falls on the stairway of Ahaz go back ten steps.’” So the sunlight went back the ten steps it had descended.
bsb.38:9: This is a writing by Hezekiah king of Judah after his illness and recovery:
bsb.38:10: I said, “In the prime of my life I must go through the gates of Sheol and be deprived of the remainder of my years.”
bsb.38:11: I said, “I will never again see the LORD, even the LORD, in the land of the living; I will no longer look on mankind with those who dwell in this world.
bsb.38:12: My dwelling has been picked up and removed from me like a shepherd’s tent. I have rolled up my life like a weaver; He cuts me off from the loom; from day until night You make an end of me.
bsb.38:13: I composed myself until the morning. Like a lion He breaks all my bones; from day until night You make an end of me.
bsb.38:14: I chirp like a swallow or crane; I moan like a dove. My eyes grow weak as I look upward. O Lord, I am oppressed; be my security.”
bsb.38:15: What can I say? He has spoken to me, and He Himself has done this. I will walk slowly all my years because of the anguish of my soul.
bsb.38:16: O Lord, by such things men live, and in all of them my spirit finds life. You have restored me to health and have let me live.
bsb.38:17: Surely for my own welfare I had such great anguish; but Your love has delivered me from the pit of oblivion, for You have cast all my sins behind Your back.
bsb.38:18: For Sheol cannot thank You; Death cannot praise You. Those who descend to the Pit cannot hope for Your faithfulness.
bsb.38:19: The living, only the living, can thank You, as I do today; fathers will tell their children about Your faithfulness.
bsb.38:20: The LORD will save me; we will play songs on stringed instruments all the days of our lives in the house of the LORD.
bsb.38:21: Now Isaiah had said, “Prepare a lump of pressed figs and apply it to the boil, and he will recover.”
bsb.38:22: And Hezekiah had asked, “What will be the sign that I will go up to the house of the LORD?”
bsb.39:1: At that time Merodach-baladan son of Baladan king of Babylon sent letters and a gift to Hezekiah, for he had heard about Hezekiah’s illness and recovery.
bsb.39:2: And Hezekiah welcomed the envoys gladly and showed them what was in his treasure house—the silver, the gold, the spices, and the precious oil, as well as his entire armory—all that was found in his storehouses. There was nothing in his palace or in all his dominion that Hezekiah did not show them.
bsb.39:3: Then the prophet Isaiah went to King Hezekiah and asked, “Where did those men come from, and what did they say to you?” “They came to me from a distant land,” Hezekiah replied, “from Babylon.”
bsb.39:4: “What have they seen in your palace?” Isaiah asked. “They have seen everything in my palace,” answered Hezekiah. “There is nothing among my treasures that I did not show them.”
bsb.39:5: Then Isaiah said to Hezekiah, “Hear the word of the LORD of Hosts:
bsb.39:6: The time will surely come when everything in your palace and all that your fathers have stored up until this day will be carried off to Babylon. Nothing will be left, says the LORD.
bsb.39:7: And some of your descendants, your own flesh and blood, will be taken away to be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.”
bsb.39:8: But Hezekiah said to Isaiah, “The word of the LORD that you have spoken is good.” For he thought, “At least there will be peace and security in my lifetime.”
bsb.40:1: “Comfort, comfort My people,” says your God.
bsb.40:2: “Speak tenderly to Jerusalem, and proclaim to her that her forced labor has been completed; her iniquity has been pardoned. For she has received from the hand of the LORD double for all her sins.”
bsb.40:3: A voice of one calling: “Prepare the way for the LORD in the wilderness; make a straight highway for our God in the desert.
bsb.40:4: Every valley shall be lifted up, and every mountain and hill made low; the uneven ground will become smooth, and the rugged land a plain.
